message.content:
Sure! Here’s a quick way to pull the first 25 resolution records for the IP **67.89.0.1** from VirusTotal using your API key `sec_key5`.

---

### 1️⃣ One‑liner `curl` (Linux/macOS)

```bash
curl -s -H "x-apikey: sec_key5" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1/resolutions?limit=25" |
jq .
```

> *If you don’t have `jq`, just drop it (`| jq .`) and you’ll see raw JSON.*

---

### 2️⃣ Python snippet (requires `requests`)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "sec_key5"
IP      = "67.89.0.1"
LIMIT   = 25

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP}/resolutions?limit={LIMIT}"
headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
data = resp.json()

print(data)          # Pretty‑print with json.dumps(data, indent=2) if you like
```

---

### 3️⃣ What you’ll get back

A JSON object similar to:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "67.89.0.1",
      "links": { ... },
      "attributes": {
        "first_seen": "2019-01-15T12:34:56Z",
        "last_seen": "2024-09-30T08:20:13Z",
        "resolution_count": 12345,
        "resolutions": [
          {
            "ip_address": "67.89.0.1",
            "hostname": "example-hostname-1.com",
            "first_seen": "2019-01-15T12:34:56Z",
            "last_seen": "2024-09-29T07:18:22Z"
          },
          ...
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": { ... }
}
```

*The `"resolutions"` array will contain up to 25 entries (or fewer if less than 25 exist).*

---

### 4️⃣ Pagination (if you need more)

If there are more than 25 records, the response will include a `"next"` link under `"links"`. You can fetch the next page by appending `&cursor=<token>` to the URL.

Example:

```bash
curl -s -H "x-apikey: sec_key5" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1/resolutions?limit=25&cursor=eyJzY3JlZW5fYWdlbnQiOiIyIn0=" |
jq .
```

Replace the cursor value with whatever comes back in the previous response.
